label: Formulated the inferiority complex and compensatory striving for superiority
description: Alfred Adler formulated Individual Psychology centered on feelings of inferiority and the vital balance of social interest.
historicalContext: Presented in 'The Neurotic Constitution' (1912) and refined in 'Understanding Human Nature' (1927).
dialecticalTension: Harmonizing personal teleological striving for mastery with Gemeinschaftsgefühl (community feeling).

label: Broke with Freud's pan-sexual libido theory, asserting the primacy of ego striving and inferiority
description: Adler broke from the Vienna Psychoanalytic Society in 1911, rejecting Freud's infantile sexual etiology in favor of teleological striving and social factors.
historicalContext: Adler resigned as president of the Vienna Psychoanalytic Society in 1911 to establish the Society for Free Psychoanalysis (Individual Psychology).
dialecticalTension: Biological causal drive determinism (Freud) versus teleological, purposive style of life oriented toward future goals (Adler).

citations.author: Henri F. Ellenberger
citations.sectionOrPage: Chapter 8: Alfred Adler and Individual Psychology

label: Adler's individual psychology directly served as the second Viennese school precursor to logotherapy
description: Viktor Frankl studied closely with Adler and published his first academic paper in Adler's International Journal of Individual Psychology.
historicalContext: Frankl was part of Adler's inner circle in the 1920s before developing logotherapy (the 'Third Viennese School').
dialecticalTension: Expanding Adler's striving for superiority into the existential 'will to meaning'.

citations.author: Viktor Frankl
citations.sectionOrPage: Part Two: Logotherapy in a Nutshell

label: Adlerian holistic style of life and phenomenological client understanding shaped Rogers
description: Carl Rogers encountered Adlerian methods at the Institute for Child Guidance in New York, shaping his person-centered therapy.
historicalContext: Adler's public clinical demonstrations in New York during the late 1920s profoundly impacted Rogers' clinical orientation.
dialecticalTension: From authoritative Adlerian lifestyle assessment toward non-directive unconditional positive regard.
